ww.Proliferative endometrium: Proliferative glands are straight and tubular with mitoses and no vacuoles, reflecting estradiol without progesterone.
ww.Atrophic endometrium: Atrophic endometrium has sparse, small, inactive glands in a thin stroma, as after menopause.
ww.Endometrial hyperplasia: Hyperplasia shows crowded glands with a high gland-to-stroma ratio from unopposed estrogen, not coiled secretory glands.
ww.Decidualized endometrium of pregnancy: Decidua shows large polygonal stromal cells with abundant cytoplasm under sustained progesterone and hCG.

look: Coiled, saw-toothed glands with vacuoles under the nuclei and an edematous stroma. These are progesterone effects, so they mark the luteal phase and are indirect evidence that ovulation occurred.
cred: Synthetic test image made for the engine test bed

ann.l: Secretory glands. Coiled, saw-toothed glands appear after ovulation because progesterone switches the endometrium from growth to secretion.
Subnuclear vacuoles. Glycogen collects below the nuclei a few days after ovulation, the earliest progesterone effect in the glands.
Edematous stroma. Late in the luteal phase the stroma swells, preparing a receptive bed for implantation.
Gland lumen with secretions. Glycogen-rich secretions move into the lumen, food for an embryo before the placenta forms.
Magnified gland cell. Enlarged here, the vacuole sits between the nucleus and the basement membrane, which is what subnuclear means.
